note: Adapted from Snyder's 1955 original English description; the original is in English and describes the female alate (type locality Rosario, Lake Romagna, Bolivia; collected in November 1921 (month 11) by W. M. Mann; the syntype is an alate); the original notes that the species had earlier (Snyder 1926) been misidentified as A. pacificus Fr. Müller, and the specific name honours E. L. Bruce.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate smaller than A. pacificus, fontanelle (transparent) smaller, ocelli larger and closer to the eyes; its position in the key close to A. pacificus. Snyder 1926 had misidentified this insect as A. pacificus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Female: head dark chestnut brown, densely covered with long hairs. Fontanelle transparent, circular. Eyes black, nearly circular, projecting; ocelli nearly elliptical, upper margin projecting, distance to the eyes slightly less than their long diameter. Postclypeus pale chestnut brown, bilobed, projecting, covered with long hairs. Antennae yellowish brown, 15-segmented, segment 3 short. Pronotum slightly paler than the head, saddle-shaped, sides smoothly rounded to the posterior margin, densely covered with long hairs. Wings smoky grey; media of the forewing nearer the cubitus than the subcosta, with 2 branches reaching the wing apex; cubitus with 10 branches reaching the lower wing margin, its width occupying half the wing. Legs yellowish brown. Abdominal tergites chestnut brown, covered with long hairs. Measurements (mm): alate total length 14.00; dealate adult length 7.50; head length (to the apex of the labrum) 1.70; pronotum length (to the anterior corner) 0.80; forewing length 12.00; hind tibia length 1.50; eye long diameter 0.25; head width (at the eyes) 1.40; pronotum width 1.40; forewing width 3.00.
